statement: Whenever can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns a result r, r is true if and only if there exist an integer d and a bijection p from the set {0,...,len(arr)-1} to itself such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1, arr[p(i+1)] - arr[p(i)] = d. Equivalently, the entries p(0),...,p(len(arr)-1) are a rearrangement of arr whose consecutive differences are all equal to d.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000 (arr[i] is interpreted as the mathematical integer value of the 64-bit element).

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, the call can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns a result r; it does not fail, overflow, panic, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions and every slice arr2 such that len(arr2) = len(arr), every element of arr2 lies in [-1000000,1000000], and arr2 is a rearrangement of arr (there is a bijection q with arr2[i] = arr[q(i)] for all i), if can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns r and can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr2) returns r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every integer c such that -1000000 <= arr[i] + c <= 1000000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), let arr2 be the slice of the same length with arr2[i] = arr[i] + c for all i. If can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns r and can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr2) returns r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every nonzero integer k such that -1000000 <= k * arr[i] <= 1000000 for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), let arr2 be the slice of the same length with arr2[i] = k * arr[i] for all i. If can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns r and can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr2) returns r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, if there exist values x and y with x != y such that every element arr[i] is equal to either x or y, and both x and y occur among the elements, then whenever can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns a result r, r is false.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 3; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, whenever can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns a result r and r is true, either arr[i] = arr[j] for all i and j with 0 <= i,j < len(arr), or arr[i] != arr[j] for all i and j with 0 <= i < j < len(arr).
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, whenever can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns a result r and r is true, let m be the minimum of arr[i] over 0 <= i < len(arr) and M be the maximum of arr[i] over 0 <= i < len(arr); then M - m is divisible by len(arr) - 1.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, let s be any sequence of length len(arr) that is a nondecreasing rearrangement of arr. Whenever can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns a result r and r is true, for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1 we have s[i+1] - s[i] = s[1] - s[0].
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every arr satisfying the preconditions, let s be any sequence of length len(arr) that is a nondecreasing rearrangement of arr. If for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr)-1 we have s[i+1] - s[i] = s[1] - s[0], then whenever can_make_arithmetic_progression(arr) returns a result r, r is true.
preconditions: len(arr) >= 2; len(arr) <= 1000; and for every i with 0 <= i < len(arr), -1000000 <= arr[i] <= 1000000.
